sources.entry: Duplicati | Encrypted, incremental backups to cloud storage and remote servers

summary.one_liner: Duplicati is a free, open-source backup client that stores encrypted, incremental, compressed backups on cloud storage services and remote file servers.
summary.what_it_does: Creates encrypted backups using AES-256 (or GNU Privacy Guard) before upload, so data stored remotely is protected. After the initial full backup, later backups are incremental/differential to save bandwidth and storage. It supports many destinations named in the README, including Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Dropbox, Google Drive, Microsoft Azure, OneDrive, FTP, WebDAV, and SSH (SFTP). A built-in scheduler runs backups automatically, and filters allow backing up folders, file types, or custom selections. It can back up open or locked files using VSS on Windows or LVM on Linux. It is available as a desktop application or a command-line tool.
use_cases: encrypted offsite backups to cloud storage
backing up files to an FTP or SFTP server
backing up to Amazon S3 or Backblaze B2
backing up locked or open files on Windows or Linux
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the Duplicati download page (the README links to it; no specific commands given).
stack: web UI (now in separate duplicati/ngclient repository)
notable: Client-side AES-256 or GnuPG encryption before any data leaves the machine
Incremental backups after an initial full backup
Volume Shadow Copy (VSS) on Windows and LVM on Linux for open or locked files
Core under MIT license; proprietary/ folder under a separate Duplicati Inc license
caveats: The proprietary/ folder is covered by a separate Duplicati Inc license rather than MIT
Web UI now lives in a separate repository (duplicati/ngclient)
Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux only as named in the README
